sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: Sum total of all **biotic** (living) and **abiotic** (non-living) elements surrounding an organism.
Resources derived from nature that exist without human intervention, categorized as **renewable** and **non-renewable**.
Celebrated globally on **5th June** every year; established in **1972** by the **UN General Assembly**.
Coinage of ecosystem done by **A.G. Tansley** in **1935**; term 'Ecology' coined by **Ernst Haeckel** in **1869**.
High-scoring core section carrying questions on **pollution acts**, **national parks**, **renewable energy targets**, and **ecological pyramids**.
Includes **10% Energy Flow Law** (Lindeman), **Biotic succession**, and **Biogeochemical cycles** (Carbon, Nitrogen, Water).
Air, Water, Soil, Noise, Radioactive, and Plastic pollution along with major international protocols like **Kyoto Protocol** and **Paris Agreement**.
Focuses on **In-situ** (National Parks, Sanctuaries) and **Ex-situ** (Botanical Gardens, Zoos, Gene banks) conservation methods.

items.title: 1. Ecosystem Structure and Energy Flow
items.content:
• **Biotic Components:** Producers (Autotrophs like green plants), Consumers (Heterotrophs - Herbivores, Carnivores, Omnivores), and Decomposers (Saprotrophs like fungi and bacteria).
• **Abiotic Components:** Climatic factors (light, temperature, humidity) and Edaphic factors (soil, minerals, pH).
• **10% Law of Energy:** Proposed by **Raymond Lindeman (1942)**; only **10%** of energy is transferred to the next trophic level, while **90%** is lost as heat.
• **Mnemonic:** **'P-C-D Eat 10 Percent'** (Producers, Consumers, Decomposers follow 10 percent energy rule).

items.title: 2. Ecological Pyramids
items.content:
• **Pyramid of Number:** Can be upright (Grassland ecosystem) or inverted (Parasitic food chain).
• **Pyramid of Biomass:** Usually upright (Terrestrial) but **inverted** in aquatic ecosystems (Phytoplankton to Zooplankton to Fish).
• **Pyramid of Energy:** **Always upright** because energy loss occurs at each successive trophic level.
• **Mnemonic:** **'Energy is Always UP'** (Pyramid of Energy is always upright).

items.title: 3. Biodiversity and Conservation Strategies
items.content:
• **Alpha Diversity:** Species diversity within a particular area or ecosystem.
• **Beta Diversity:** Comparison of species diversity between ecosystems.
• **Gamma Diversity:** Diversity of the entire landscape or geographical region.
• **In-situ Conservation:** Protecting species in their natural habitat (**National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, Biosphere Reserves**).
• **Ex-situ Conservation:** Protecting species outside their natural habitat (**Zoos, Botanical Gardens, Seed Banks, Cryopreservation**).

items.title: 4. Environmental Pollution and Global Issues
items.content:
• **Air Pollution:** Major pollutants include **SO2, NO2, CO, PM2.5, PM10, and Ozone (tropospheric)**.
• **Water Pollution:** Measured via **BOD** (Biochemical Oxygen Demand) and **COD** (Chemical Oxygen Demand); high BOD indicates severe organic pollution.
• **Global Warming & Greenhouse Effect:** Key gases include **CO2, CH4, N2O, CFCs, and Water Vapor** (CO2 has the highest absolute contribution, CFCs have highest warming potential per molecule).
• **Ozone Depletion:** Occurs mainly in the **Stratosphere** due to **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)** releasing Chlorine free radicals.

items.title: 5. Important Environmental Legislation in India
items.content:
• **Wildlife Protection Act:** Enacted in **1972**.
• **Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act:** Enacted in **1974**.
• **Forest (Conservation) Act:** Enacted in **1980**.
• **Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act:** Enacted in **1981**.
• **Environment (Protection) Act:** Enacted in **1986** (umbrella legislation).
• **National Biodiversity Act:** Enacted in **2002**.

sections.title: Important Facts and Data
rows: Term coined by **Ernst Haeckel** in **1869**; study of organisms and environment.
Concept given by **Norman Myers (1988)**; total **36** global hotspots (India has **4**).
Nutrient enrichment of water bodies leading to algal bloom and oxygen depletion.
Signed in **1971** in Iran for wetland conservation; India has **75+** Ramsar sites.
Signed in **1987** (effective **1989**) for protection of the **Ozone layer**.
Adopted in **1997** (COP 3); legally binding targets for greenhouse gas reduction.
Adopted in **2015** (COP 21); aims to keep global temperature rise well below **2°C**.
Target to achieve **500 GW** non-fossil energy capacity by **2030**.
**Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve** established in **1986** in India.

items.definition: Use the acronym **'H-W-E-N'**: **H**imalayas, **W**estern Ghats, **E**astern Himalayas / Indo-Burma, **N**icobar Islands (Sundaland).
Remember sequence **'Wild Water Forest Air Environment'**: Wildlife (**1972**), Water (**1974**), Forest (**1980**), Air (**1981**), Environment (**1986**).

Use acronym **'MEANS'**: **M**ethane, **E**thene (Water vapor/ozone), **A**rgon (not greenhouse, skip), **N**itrous oxide, **S**arban dioxide (Carbon dioxide). Simplified: **CO2, CH4, N2O, CFCs, Water Vapor**.
Remember **'P-H-C-T'**: **P**rimary Producers -> **H**erbivores (Primary Consumers) -> **C**arnivores (Secondary Consumers) -> **T**op Carnivores.
**In-situ** = **In** natural home (National Parks). **Ex-situ** = **Exit** home to a new artificial place (Zoos, Botanical Gardens).
Only **Aquatic Ecosystem** has inverted biomass pyramid because phytoplankton reproduce rapidly but have small individual biomass compared to zooplankton/fish.

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Ecology vs Ecosystem terms
items.definition: **Ernst Haeckel** coined 'Ecology' (**1869**), whereas **A.G. Tansley** coined 'Ecosystem' (**1935**). Do not interchange their names.
Students often think energy pyramids can be inverted. Remember that the **Pyramid of Energy is ALWAYS upright** due to thermodynamic laws (Lindeman's 10% law).
Ozone layer is primarily found in the **Stratosphere** (specifically 15-35 km altitude), NOT in the Troposphere where it acts as a harmful pollutant.

items.term: Mistake 4: Montreal vs Kyoto Protocol mix-up
items.definition: **Montreal Protocol (1987)** is strictly for **Ozone depleting substances (CFCs)**, while **Kyoto Protocol (1997)** is for **Greenhouse gases/Climate change**.

items.term: Mistake 5: Biosphere reserve vs National park count
items.definition: India has **18 Biosphere Reserves** (12 recognized under UNESCO MAB program), and over **106 National Parks**. Do not confuse these numbers.
High BOD means **Low Dissolved Oxygen (DO)** and high water pollution. Students incorrectly assume high BOD means high pure oxygen.
Comprises all living (**biotic**) and non-living (**abiotic**) factors interacting in a dynamic system.
Functional unit of nature comprising biotic community and its abiotic environment interacting as a system.
Only **10%** energy passes from one trophic level to the next; **90%** is lost as metabolic heat.
Nutrients move through biotic and abiotic components; examples include **Carbon, Nitrogen, and Hydrological cycles**.
Must contain at least **1,500 species of vascular plants** as endemics and have lost at least **70%** of its original habitat.
Famous forest conservation movement in **1973** in Uttarakhand led by **Sunderlal Bahuguna** and **Chandi Prasad Bhatt**.
Environmental movement in **1973-1984** in Kerala to protect tropical evergreen rainforests from a hydroelectric dam project.
National Parks have stricter regulations with **no human activity or grazing allowed**, unlike sanctuaries where limited activities are permitted.
Wetlands of international importance designated under the **Ramsar Convention (1971)**.
Include **Solar, Wind, Hydroelectric, Geothermal, Biomass, and Tidal energy** which are inexhaustible.
Include **Coal, Petroleum, Natural Gas, and Nuclear minerals (Uranium)** which take millions of years to form.
Accumulation of toxic substances (like **DDT or Mercury**) in increasing concentrations at successive trophic levels.

upscNotes.content: For the UP Assistant Teacher Exam, memorize the exact enactment years of environmental laws (1972, 1974, 1980, 1981, 1986) as direct chronological questions are frequently asked.
Pay close attention to international protocols (Montreal, Kyoto, Ramsar, Paris Agreement) along with their target years and primary objectives.
Questions often confuse 'Biomagnification' (toxin concentration increase up the food chain) with 'Bioaccumulation' (toxin buildup in a single organism over time). Read options carefully.
Do not confuse the inventor of 'Ecology' (Ernst Haeckel) with 'Ecosystem' (A.G. Tansley) or 'Deep Ecology' (Arne Naess).

keyTakeaways: Ecosystem energy flow follows the 10% law established by Lindeman in 1942.
India possesses 4 recognized biodiversity hotspots out of 36 global hotspots.
Environmental Protection Act of 1986 acts as the umbrella legislation in India.
Pyramid of energy is always upright, whereas biomass pyramid can be inverted in aquatic systems.
Montreal Protocol (1987) targets Ozone Depletion; Kyoto Protocol (1997) targets Greenhouse Gases.
In-situ conservation protects species in natural habitats, while Ex-situ uses artificial settings like zoos and botanical gardens.
